units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 7:24">Targ. Prov. VII, 24</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Shabbat 91a:6">Sabb. 91ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>בתר ה׳ אזלינן</he> we go by the present condition.
<cite ref="Pesachim 4a:5">Pes. 4ᵃ</cite> <he>וה׳ דקי״ל</he> and now that it is established that &c.
Ḥull. 97ᵃ ה׳ דאמר וכ׳ now that R. … says &c.; a. v. fr.—הכי ה׳ so now!, indeed, i.e. how can you compare these two cases? Snh. 41ᵇ; a. fr.—2) (introducing an argument) since, when, if.

<cite ref="Chullin 5b:10">Ḥull. 5ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>ה׳ בהמתן … לא כל שכן</he> since the Lord does not allow any evil to come through a beast belonging to the righteous, how much less through the righteous themselves? <cite ref="Chullin 6b:4">Ib. 6ᵇ</cite> <he>ה׳ מיגזל גזלה חלופי מיבעיא</he> if she would take what is not her own, is there any question that she would eventually exchange her own for what belongs to her neighbor?; a. fr.
